abstract: We extend restrictions on positive rational shortcut-Collatz orbits from automatic parity and two primitive-substitution classes to every coded primitive fixed word. The new complete written proof candidate states that primitive substitutive parity forces an eventually periodic orbit, allowing finite shifts and prepended words. It includes reducible incidence polynomials with noninteger Perron roots. The automatic theorem and the earlier irreducible and integer-Perron cases remain. We split the rational Perron primary component from the subdominant invariant space. A positive unimodular cone supplies an integral fast basis after a substitution power; the slow prefix exponents have sublinear support and their algebraic parameters may be nonunits. Relative formal regularity is proved using a Laurent valuation, degree preservation under monomial base change, a Newton-polytope argument for branch divisors, purity, and the classical classification of finite étale torus covers. The local relation-matrix argument keeps its coefficient field fixed before auxiliary degrees and absorbs slow contributions uniformly over the analytic tail. Algebraic primitive frequencies and Gelfond–Schneider give the strict density gap required to compare real and 2-adic inverse-parity values. Seven exact CPU audits support finite interfaces only; the new suite checks five reducible noninteger-Perron presentations. The new analytic arguments remain independently unreviewed and formally unverified. The revision also addresses the earlier review's bibliographic request concerning López–Stoll's broader2021claim and its unproved transfer between completions. No general morphic classification, arbitrary-integer parity structure, exclusion of other positive cycles, or solution of Collatz follows.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds Theorem1d and Sections15–17 for all coded primitive fixed words, including reducible noninteger-Perron incidence matrices. Supplies a positive fast-lattice basis construction, a relative formal regularity proof via monomial degree preservation, ramification and étale torus covers, and the full local fast/slow specialization and consumer. Adds one five-worker audit of five new three-letter cases; all six previous source/result pairs are unchanged. Also addresses v1 review feedback by discussing López–Stoll2021 and the completion-transfer gap, comparing the periodic-dictionary result, and removing stale drafting labels. The new extension has not been independently or formally verified. Credits Fourier Wren's sharper elementary rational-point factor-complexity bound and distinguishes that deduction from the algebraic-irrational content of the earlier Subspace criterion. No proof of the general primitive extension or audit source/output is changed by this attribution update.
title: Automatic parity and primitive substitutions in rational Collatz dynamics
